description: OTAWA static WCET targets for sertos_stm32g070 (functions from ../1.csv).

timing.clock_notes: SystemClock_Config: HSI16, PLL off, AHB/APB prescaler 1, FLASH_LATENCY_0. Profiler timer runs at PCLK1 = 16 MHz, so profiler cycles equal CPU cycles.
timing.reduce_irreducible_loops_notes: libgcc __udivsi3 (Cortex-M0+ has no hardware divider) contains an irreducible loop; OTAWA REDUCED_LOOPS_FEATURE is required to bound it.

m0plus.notes: Cortex-M0+ cycle table (Arm DDI 0484C) implemented by the m0plus/ OTAWA plugin: ALU 1, LDR/STR 2, PUSH/LDM/STM 1+N, POP 1+N (3+N with PC), B/BX/BLX 2, BL 3, B<cond> 1 (+taken_branch_penalty on taken edges), MRS/MSR/barriers 4. mul_cycles 1 assumes the fast multiplier (use 32 for the small one). mem_wait_states 0: FLASH_LATENCY_0 at 16 MHz; peripheral bus wait states are not modelled.

trivial.notes: Fixed cost per instruction. Cortex-M0+ (0 wait states) needs 1 cycle for ALU ops and 2 for loads/stores and taken branches, so 2 is the per-instruction upper estimate. 1 cycle under-estimates measured maxima (sertos_task_create_static, sertos_scheduler_init_with_config); the 'generic' model is safe but ~3.7x more pessimistic.

generic.notes: Cortex-M0+ two-stage pipeline with 0-wait-state flash at 16 MHz.

instrumentation.notes: The Debug ELF is instrumented (-finstrument-functions). Profiler cycles include the hooks of nested instrumented calls, so hooks are analysed by default. Set to false to exclude them (nocall).

multicalls.reason: Only reachable from sertos_stats_reset() inside sertos_scheduler_init_with_config(), whose visitor is reset_visitor.

loops.reason: Retry loop. Producer passes SERTOS_NO_WAIT, so the body returns TIMEOUT before the back edge.
Retry loop. Single consumer with SERTOS_WAIT_FOREVER: after wake-up data is present, so at most one re-check. Blocking time is not execution time.
linked_list_init over SERTOS_CONFIG_MAX_PRIORITIES = 32.
libgcc 64-bit shift/subtract division (SERTOS_MS_TO_TICKS): at most 64 iterations.
libgcc 32-bit division processes the dividend 8 bits per iteration: at most 4 iterations.
Wait list length <= number of tasks (idle, producer, consumer, profiler).
newlib-nano byte loop; ring buffer copies at most item_size = sizeof(SertosDemoQueueItem) = 4 bytes.
newlib-nano byte loop; largest painted task stack is SERTOS_PROF_STACK_BYTES = 2048.
32 priorities -> 1 bitmap word.
32 priorities -> 1 bitmap word (loop over remaining words runs 0 times).
During scheduler init only the idle task is registered.
Calls are well nested per context (captures report 0 stale frames): the matching shadow-stack frame is on top, found in the first iteration.
Legacy single-stack compaction; unused once contexts are registered (switch hook), and the matching frame is on top, so no frames are shifted.
Context table scan <= PROFILER_CONTEXT_CAPACITY = 6 slots (cache miss).
Free-slot scan <= PROFILER_CONTEXT_CAPACITY = 6 slots.

Only the idle task is created: SERTOS_CONFIG_IDLE_TASK_STACK_SIZE = 512 bytes painted.

blocking_bound.reason: Consumer (prio 2) waits forever for the producer (prio 3, delay_ms(10) period, NO_WAIT send). Next item arrives <= 10 ticks after the previous one plus the producer's release jitter (one producer job); after the send the consumer still waits for the producer to block (second job). PendSV: switch to producer, to consumer, plus one in-progress switch. extra_cycles: inline producer loop code (<= 50 instructions x 2 cycles) per job. Assumes the producer is not paused (B1 not pressed).
Wrapper of sertos_queue_receive called by the consumer task: same blocking scenario.

Worst caller is the profiler task (prio 1, lowest) with delay(10); the producer calls it through delay_ms(10) and is covered by that bound. Producer and consumer (period 10 ticks) can each run one job before the wake-up tick is computed and one after the wake-up. PendSV: three switches per burst. extra_cycles: inline producer and consumer loop code (<= 50 instructions x 2 cycles) per job.
Only the producer (prio 3, highest application task) calls delay_ms(10) = SERTOS_MS_TO_TICKS(10) = 10 ticks. No task preempts it; PendSV: switch back to the producer plus one in-progress switch.

loops.reason: Delay list holds at most the three application tasks (producer, consumer, profiler); idle never delays.
The application creates no software timers: the active timer list is empty.

interference_functions.name: PendSV_Handler
interference_functions.reason: Context switch (includes the profiler switch hook); counted per switch in blocking_bound.interference.

interference_notes: Analysed by wcet_csv.py (rows appended to 1w.csv) but not compared against captures. Entries with period_cycles are periodic ISRs used by compare_csv.py as ceil(R_post / period) + 1 activations in the response-time bound. USART2 and DMA ISRs only run while a dump command is being served and are excluded.
blocking_bound_notes: Response-time bound for WALL-mode captures of blocking functions: R = blocked_ticks * cpu_clock_hz / tick_hz + R_post, with R_post = WCET(self) + sum(count * WCET(function)) + extra_cycles + sum over periodic ISRs of (ceil(R_post / period_cycles) + 1) * WCET(isr), iterated to a fixed point. compare_csv.py checks target WALL max <= R.
measured_includes_blocking_notes: WALL-mode captures (PROFILER_APP_TIME_MODE=WALL, default) of these functions include the time the task is blocked (queue wait or delay). compare_csv.py checks their ACTIVE-mode maximum (--target-active, 1a.csv) against the WCET and their WALL maximum against the blocking_bound response-time bound.
